_about: Measured cost/memory coefficients for nvalchemi-toolkit + FairChem UMA, used by plan_run.py. Every number is from a real run; see benchmark/uma_efficiency/README.md for the derivations. Recalibrate by re-running the efficiency matrix (run_efficiency_matrix.sh) and refitting (README.md, 'Recalibrating').

reference.system: Au-Pt fcc, a = 4.00 A, 500 atoms (5x5x5 conventional cells), 1200 K
reference.measured: 2026-09-24..30, efficiency matrix (500 atoms, widths 1/2/4) + follow-up (widths 8/12, 108/256/2048 atoms, checkpointing, compile), A100-SXM4-80GB

time_model._form: one batched step takes c1_ms_per_atom * (n0_atoms + width * (N_eff * sf + nw_atoms)) ms on the reference GPU: n0 = per-call overhead in atom-equivalents (amortized by batching), nw = per-walker overhead (not amortized), sf = size_scaling factor, applied to compiled runs only. Least-squares fit (relative error) to every A100-SXM cell of the efficiency matrix and its follow-up: 108-2048 atoms, widths 1-16.

memory_model._form: peak reserved GiB = base_gib + per_walker_gib * A + per_walker_cross_gib * A * (width - 1), A = width * N_eff / 500 (memory is linear in atom count; no size ramp). The cross term is non-zero only for SGC-NPT, whose memory grows faster than linear in the number of walkers. budget_scale lowers the usable fraction of the card for families the fit under-predicts.

size_scaling._note: Applied to compiled per-atom TIME only: one large graph costs more per atom under compile (Kawasaki turbo: 79 ms/step for 2048 atoms x 1 vs 58 ms for 500 x 4). Memory has no size ramp: it is linear in atom count (measured 108-2048 atoms).
